# Additive tuning of 2026-11-06, mcp round 1 best so far, scenario 5

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
```

**This line is the `best` stage of round 1 of the MCP layer, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1880](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880) asked for.** It measures scenario 5, the documents, the engine and the MCP server as they stand, before any change to the server is screened. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-5 tuning`. It is the `scenario-5` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288. The owner accepted the plan of this layer [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6655760192).

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `cce750f7` for the whole batch. The base it is read against is scenario 2 at `329f3362`, which the owner adopted from the engine layer [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6656833332). The engine changes since that pin are the recorder and grader changes of #1932 and #1933, which the owner accepted against this base on #1879 ([comment 6619960661](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879#issuecomment-6619960661) and [comment 6623069015](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1879#issuecomment-6623069015)). The canary of 8 sessions cost 654 cents, and seven of its sessions called the MCP server. It held 5 records that named a path outside the workspace, each for a `find /` search for a file the session could not find. The sandbox binds none of those paths. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1880#issuecomment-6667551725). The driver then halted on the plan's usage limits, first with 79 and then with 118 of 154 sessions recorded. The last halted sessions failed on the plan's 5-hour limit and then on its 7-day limit, and the driver's own usage gate did not stop the batch. Each halted session was recorded again from the start once the limit reset, in the same try root at the same pin. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 13540 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 3 stopped at the turn cap, 0 stopped at the session budget, 142 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. 101 of the 154 sessions used the MCP layer. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 5 passed 116 of the 154 sessions it graded, 75%. The base, scenario 2, passed 112 of 154, 73%, over the same 22 probes in [the engine layer's transcript](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-02-engine-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-2.md). The difference is +2.6 points, with the interval [-7.2, +12.3]. The interval includes zero by a wide margin, so this batch does not show that the MCP server adds to the documents and the engine. The keep rule reads only a confirmation, and a best so far is never kept. This line is the number that each screened change of the MCP layer is compared with.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 15000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 14225 cents against its cap. The 154 recorded sessions account for 13540 cents, the 654 cents of the canary included. The other 685 cents are the partial cost of the sessions that the usage limits stopped, which the driver recorded again. The first best so far of a layer is charged to the base ceiling, so `try.sh spent` counts the 14225 cents against the base ceiling of 30000 cents.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1880/mcp-r1-best/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.
